A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe the same RDD research and include supplementary Sections 7–10. Their text, equations, seven figures and ten tables are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original pose-estimation, homography, localization and ablation results in Tables 1–5, with additional matching experiments and runtime measurements in supplementary Tables 6–10.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including RDD benchmark scores, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary detector/descriptor comparisons.

M1.justification: The two-branch architecture, deformable attention, keypoint detection, sparse matching, semi-dense epipolar refinement and training objectives in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MegaDepth and Air-to-Ground training data and retain evaluation on MegaDepth-1500, MegaDepth-View, Air-to-Ground, HPatches and Aachen Day-Night. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator rows remain identical within every main and supplementary experiment, including the DeDoDe variants, ALIKED, XFeat, dense methods and learned matchers. The added SIFT citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training schedules, dataset construction, image resizing, keypoint budgets, evaluation metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. The supplementary LO-RANSAC and detector/descriptor combination settings were already present in v4.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains the same architecture, training, refinement and training-data ablations. The supplementary qualitative comparisons, runtime analysis, LO-RANSAC experiment and detector/descriptor combinations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without disclosed evaluation run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries, and the qualitative matching examples are unchanged. For example, RDD's MegaDepth-1500 AUCs remain 48.2/65.2/78.3 in Table 1, while the LO-RANSAC results remain 62.9/75.8/85.1 in supplementary Table 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20, including the attention, keypoint, refinement and loss definitions, are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric robustness, global context, sparse and semi-dense matching, performance and the two contributed benchmarks.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning absent explicit data augmentation and reliance on confident sparse correspondences, which can cause semi-dense matching failures.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, data collection and preprocessing instructions, H100 training information and RTX 4090 timing information are unchanged. The project-page access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Lowe's 2004 SIFT paper as reference [28] and cites it in the introductory SIFT discussion, where v4 cited SIFT Flow [25]. SIFT Flow remains elsewhere; other reference updates concern existing works' publication metadata rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 expands or revises bibliographic details for existing references, including Key.Net, SiLK, ResNet, DISK and ALIKED, and updates citation numbering and the version/date stamp. The research prose and main/supplementary section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded reference entries cause limited bibliography reflow across PDF pages 12–14. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–10 retain their visual content, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: Replacing the introductory SIFT Flow citation with Lowe's SIFT paper and supplying fuller publication details modestly improve attribution and reference completeness. The scientific content and empirical support are unchanged. The attribution correction remains incomplete because Section 2 still cites SIFT Flow for SIFT.
